### Observed differences

- Three activities that never appeared in the earlier window — A32, A33 and A38 — each run in about half of the later traces (roughly 98–100 of 200 cases), positioned around the middle of the trace (mean relative position about 0.51). [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- Routing out of A26 changed: earlier, about 95 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions went to A27; later, about 51 in 100 go to A27 and about 49 in 100 go to the new activities (A33 about 18, A38 about 17, A32 about 15). [DIR006]
- A27 became optional: it appeared in all 200 earlier traces but in only about 52 in 100 of the later traces. [OCC003]
- The new activities form a connected group: A32 leads mostly to A38 (about 35 in 100) and A33 (about 34), A33 leads mostly back to A32 (about 41), and A38 leads mostly to A28 (about 43) and to A33/A32. [DIR007, DIR008, DIR009]
- The distance from A26 to A28 changed: earlier the gap was almost always 2 steps (about 91 in 100); later it splits between 2 steps (about 50 in 100) and 4 steps (about 46 in 100), matching a route with three inserted activities. [LAG003]
- A04 now occurs far more often and earlier: participation rose from about 19 to 60 in 100 traces and its mean relative position moved from about 0.54 to about 0.21. A14 now leads to A04 in about 54 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 4 before), A04 leads to A15 in about 87 in 100 (before about 20, spread over many successors), A04 follows A14 within one step in about 96 in 100 of later cases, and the A14→A15 gap shifted from mostly one step (about 46 in 100) to mostly two steps (about 31 in 100). The before-side of the A14→A04 gap rests on only 14 observations. [OCC001, POS001, DIR004, DIR001, LAG001, LAG002]
- A06 nearly disappeared: from about 20 to 4 in 100 traces; its later outgoing profile rests on only 8 transitions and is not reliable. [OCC002, DIR002]
- The backbone edges A15→A16, A44→A45 and A46→A47 stayed essentially stable, and A28's position shifted only slightly later (mean about 0.53 to 0.56). [DIR005, DIR010, DIR011, POS002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

A structural possibility supported by the evidence: in the later window, a group of three previously unobserved activities (A32, A33, A38) executes between A26 and A28 as an alternative to A27 — A26 now leads either to A27 or into the new group in roughly equal shares, A27 runs in only about half of traces (down from all), and the A26→A28 gap split from almost always two steps into two- and four-step gaps that match the two routes. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, POS003, POS004, POS005, LAG003]

The supporting signs are direct participation, successor and lag evidence that all line up on the same insertion, and a qualifying-item count (25) far above the roughly 0.6 expected without change, so the set as a whole is not a sampling artefact — though items describing the same traces are not independent confirmations. Limitations: the order inside the new group varies (its members lead to one another and to A28), and the mutual exclusivity of the two routes per trace is inferred from shares summing to about 100% of A26's outgoing transitions, not observed directly. A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the new activity codes relabel existing activities rather than adding genuinely new steps. [DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, LAG003]

Other differences: A04 is now inserted between A14 and A15 in many traces — higher participation, an earlier position, A14 gaining A04 as successor while A14→A15 drops, and the A14→A15 gap moving from one to two steps; this is a second, separate structural difference. A06 was executed in only about 4 in 100 later traces (down from about 20), but the small after-support makes the detail of its redirection weak. [OCC001, POS001, DIR004, DIR001, LAG001, LAG002, OCC002, DIR002]
